guard: the continuity refusal carries the workspace renderer's remedy, and several running meshes are each reported before the install
why: #1879. With two meshes running and the shell outside both roots, update printed the resolver's bare `multiple meshes running: …` and exited 1 before writing anything. Two defects shared that line: the refusal dropped the remedy every other command renders, and a global install that every running manager shares was reported for one manager or none.
M1 restores the bare `message(e)` text. The refusal cell names the remedy sentence, so it goes red on that assertion while a non-target error still prints unchanged.
M2 removes the enumeration and rethrows. The several-managers cell observes both managers being read, so it goes red on the first read of the second manager.
M3 stops the loop at the first legacy verdict. The cell asserts both managers are still observed, which is #1620 for all of them rather than just the first.

mutations.name: M1 print the resolver's bare text instead of the rendered remedy
mutations.expectRed: the standing refusal carries the workspace renderer's remedy sentence
mutations.cell: #1879: the continuity refusal carries the workspace renderer's remedy
mutations.note: The result stays a string and every other error prints identically; only the MeshTargetError arm loses the recovery copy, which is the defect as reported.

mutations.name: M2 refuse an ambiguous target instead of reporting each running manager
mutations.expectRed: every running manager is read, in turn
mutations.cell: #1879: several running meshes report each manager's continuity in turn
mutations.note: Restores the original refusal: any ambiguous target rethrows, so no manager past the resolver is ever observed. The selected-target cells still pass, since a selected target never entered this arm.

mutations.name: M3 stop at the first legacy verdict instead of observing every manager
mutations.find:
if (await readOne({ ...flags, space }) === "legacy") verdict = "legacy";
      else console.log(c.dim("  manager custody carries this update"));
mutations.replace:
if (await readOne({ ...flags, space }) === "legacy") return "legacy";
      else console.log(c.dim("  manager custody carries this update"));
mutations.expectRed: a legacy verdict does not stop the remaining managers being observed
mutations.cell: #1879: several running meshes report each manager's continuity in turn
mutations.note: Still returns legacy for the whole run, so the verdict assertions survive. It reintroduces the partial answer from the other direction: the managers after the first legacy one are never observed, which the alpha-legacy pass catches.
